about.title: Why Ensemble exists
about.lead: People who rely on AI for answers that matter already cross-check: they paste the same question into several chatbots and try to work out which answer to trust. Ensemble does that in one step and measures the part that matters, whether the models agree.

problem.heading: A single model gives no warning
problem.body: It sounds the same whether it is right or guessing. When models from different providers give the same answer, that is a useful sign. When they disagree, no single answer should be trusted on that question.

score.heading: What the score can and cannot tell you
score.body: The score measures how close the answers are in meaning, using embeddings. Models can agree and still be wrong, for example when they learned the same mistake. Treat high agreement as a reason for more confidence, not as proof. The labels use default thresholds until each embedding model is calibrated on benchmark runs.

items.title: Cross-checkers
items.body: Research, engineering, health and legal reading, purchases: anyone who wants confidence before acting on an AI answer.

items.title: Local model users
items.body: Privacy and no cost, with models running on your own machine.

items.title: Model tinkerers
items.body: Compare models and merge methods on your own questions, with the cost of every run.

research.heading: Research on combining models
research.intro: Published work has studied several ways to combine language models. These papers report gains on their own benchmarks and settings. We have not reproduced them; our own results are on the benchmarks page.

papers.title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
papers.finding: Open-source LLM ensembles collectively surpassed GPT-4o by 7.6% on AlpacaEval 2.0.

papers.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
papers.finding: Multi-model debate improved GSM8K math accuracy from 77% to 85%.

papers.title: ReConcile: Round-Table Conference Improves Reasoning via Consensus
papers.finding: Up to 11.4% improvement over single-model baselines through structured consensus.

papers.title: Iterative Consensus Ensemble of LLMs for Medical Question Answering
papers.finding: Achieved a 23% accuracy gain on medical questions through iterative LLM consensus.

papers.title: Harnessing Multiple LLMs: A Survey on Collaboration, Competition and Synergy
papers.finding: Comprehensive taxonomy of multi-LLM collaboration strategies and their effectiveness.

about.benchmarksLink: See our benchmark method and results

features.title: Everything you need to compare AI answers
features.lead: Ensemble asks several models the same question, shows every answer side by side, measures how closely they agree and merges them into one answer. It shows you when the models disagree; it does not promise that the merged answer beats the best single model.

items.title: Answers side by side
items.body: Two to six models answer at once. Each answer streams into its own column with its time and cost, and one failed model never stops the run.

items.title: An agreement score you can read
items.body: Answers are compared pair by pair with semantic embeddings. High agreement means the models give the same answer, which is a reason for more confidence but not proof; low agreement tells you to read every answer.

items.title: One merged answer
items.body: Choose how answers are merged: Standard (one summary), Majority (a vote on short answers), Ranked (models judge each other in pairs) or Council (critique, rebuttal and a vote).

items.title: Cost before you spend it
items.body: Every method shows how many calls it makes and an estimated cost before you ask, and the real cost once the run is done.

items.title: Your own answers too
items.body: Paste an answer from another tool or an expert. It is scored and merged with the others.

items.title: Presets and history
items.body: Save a set of models and a method as a preset. Your runs are kept in this browser.

models.heading: Models from anywhere
models.intro: Use your own keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek and Perplexity, or any OpenAI-compatible server. One OpenRouter key reaches every major provider.

items.title: Cloud providers
items.body: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek and Perplexity, called straight from your browser with your keys.

items.title: Local models
items.body: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM on your machine. Ensemble finds a running Ollama for you, and a local embedding model scores agreement with no cloud key.

items.title: Hosted open models
items.body: OpenRouter, Groq, Together or any OpenAI-compatible address.

items.title: Keys stay in your browser
items.body: Keys are encrypted with AES-GCM through the Web Crypto API and sent only to each provider, never to our server.

items.title: Prompts go straight to the providers
items.body: In Free mode your questions and answers travel between your browser and the providers you pick. Our server does not see them.

items.title: Nothing leaves your machine
items.body: With local models every call, including the agreement score, stays on your computer.

items.title: Free: works today
items.body: Bring your own keys and pay the providers directly, or pay nothing with local models. No sign-in.

items.title: Pro: coming soon
items.body: Sign in, buy credits and run models without managing any key.

claims.heading: What we can and cannot claim yet
claims.body: Whether an ensemble beats its best single model is not settled. The benchmarks page describes how we test it; results will appear there once the run is done.
